newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SCORE WELL ON EMU DEFICIT AND INTEREST RATES.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SCORE WELL ON EMU DEFICIT AND INTEREST RATES.

text.p: Figures published by the Dutch
Central Planning Bureau (CPB) showed the Netherlands' performing
better than most European Union countries on two of the main
"convergence criteria" for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The CPB estimates for 1997 showed Dutch long-term interest
rates and the public sector deficit both well below the average
for the 15 European Union (EU) countries. However, inflation and
public sector debt were both slightly above the EU averages.
The table shows CPB estimates for performance on the main
EMU criteria by the Netherlands (NL), Germany (D), France (F)
and the average of all 15 EU countries.
NL EU D F NL EU D F
NOTES - Inflation shows the annual percentage rise in
consumer prices. Interest rate refers to 10-year govt bond
yields. Public sector deficit and public sector debt are
expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP).
EMU convergence criteria stipulate a maximum deficit of
three percent of GDP. Debt should be falling and approaching 60
percent of GDP at a satisfactory pace.
Inflation should be no more than 1.5 percentage points above
the average of the three EU members with the lowest inflation.
Long-term interest rates should be no more than two
percentage points above the average interest rate of the three
EU members with the lowest inflation.
